newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends lower on reduced demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends lower on reduced demand.

text.p: Indian call money eased on reduced demand to end Thursday at 5.25-5.50 percent, off the day's high of 6.50-6.75 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's trade was done between 6.0 percent and 6.5 percent, with stray deals at 6.75 percent.
"It (higher rates) was largely a reaction to yesterday's repos auction and the 10-year bond auction later today," said a dealer at a state-run bank.

The Reserve Bank of India mopped up 16.4 billion rupees at a four-day repos auction of government of India securities held on Wednesday. It auctions 10 billion rupees of 10-year bonds later on Thursday.

"The outflows towards the repos took place today," said a dealer. "Even though the payment for the bonds will be tomorrow, sentiment in the market was affected as the market expects full subscription."
He said call money rates were largely lender-driven on Thursday and came down as demand from borrowers eased later in the day.
Dealers said prices of government securities fell slightly in moderate trade.

"There were mainly sellers in the market today," said a dealer. "The high call rates could have been one reason. Further the market is also waiting to see the cut-off at the bond auction as it will signal which way long-term rates are headed."
Earlier issues of 10-year bonds in 1996/97 (April-March) were at 13.85 percent. Market participants expect a cut-off of 13.60-13.65 percent at Thursday's auction.

The 12 percent 1999 government of India stock traded on Thursday at 99.68 rupees against its last traded price of 99.72, the 13.50 percent 1997 dropped to 102.87 from 102.93 while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock eased to 101.59 from 101.62.
Treasury bills maturing in July yielded 9.25 percent against the previous yield of 9.40 percent, dealers said.
